stem: Ishaan must construct a square of side $6$ cm with ruler and compass.

options.text: Draw base AB of $6$ cm, construct a perpendicular at A and at B, mark $6$ cm on each perpendicular, and join the new ends.
Draw a base of $6$ cm and raise perpendiculars at both ends, but mark any new lengths on those uprights.
Find the area $36$ cm$^{2}$ first, and treat that area calculation as the construction.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Equal base and upright markings with right angles at both ends force all four sides equal and all angles right, which is a square.

teacher.key_rationale: A square needs equal sides and right angles: base 6 cm, perpendiculars at both ends, and 6 cm marked on each. B omits equal-length uprights. C swaps construction for an area calculation.
